title: The Patient Who Wasn't Injured
text:
A man collapsed inside Sera's tea shop without a wound.

Luo Wen — the **Laughing Undertaker**, physician and Top Ten acupoint specialist — could heal a body or shut it down with the same anatomical precision.

Luo Wen examined him first.

Pulse normal.

Breathing normal.

No poison.

No internal bleeding.

Then the man's heart stopped.

For seven seconds.

It restarted before Luo touched him.

A red mark appeared beneath his wrist.

Rhen saw it.

So did Luo.

[[speaker:luo]]“That is not natural.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“No.”

Sera recognized the expression on Rhen's face.

Another old problem.

Excellent.

The patient carried a medical token stamped with an obsolete imperial seal.

Liang Yue arrived before sunset.

This was not a new face to Sera. World #2 had already crossed her path during the Three Dukes incident. Now the Bloodless Empress was finally stepping into Sera's daily life instead of passing through it.

World #2.

No announcement.

No entourage.

The room changed anyway.

Sera had faced her once.

Years ago.

She remembered White Blood entering the air and the certainty that direct victory was impossible.

Liang looked at the red mark.

[[speaker:liang]]“Yan Shou.”

Rhen's gaze hardened.

Sera folded her arms.

[[speaker:sera]]“Good. Someone finally has a name.”

title: The Red Thread Coroner
text:
Mei Zhen introduced herself while examining a dead man's scar.

Known as **The Red Thread Coroner**, she was a forensic martial physician rather than a frontline monster. She reconstructed old injuries, poisons and technique traces from scar tissue — exactly the kind of specialist Sera needed while investigating Rhen's hidden medical interventions.

Bright red thread was wound around every finger.

Her art was Echo Beneath the Scar.

By passing minute pulses through damaged tissue, she could reconstruct old trauma from the way scarred meridians answered.

Not Top Ten.

Not close.

Still one of the best forensic physicians alive.

Mei examined Sera by request.

Then stopped talking.

Sera disliked that immediately.

[[speaker:sera]]“What?”

[[speaker:meizhen]]“Your meridians were rebuilt.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I know.”

[[speaker:meizhen]]“No. Rebuilt.”

Mei looked toward Rhen.

[[speaker:meizhen]]“These were not merely repaired. Whoever saved you corrected old inefficiencies while doing it.”

Sera slowly turned.

Rhen looked innocent.

He was terrible at it.

[[speaker:meizhen]]“This is medical cultivation beyond every modern school I know.”

Liang said nothing.

That silence confirmed more than praise would have.

title: I Did Not Spare You
text:
Sera and Liang walked the Northern Road alone.

The same road where Sera had collapsed years earlier after crossing three Dukes.

Sera finally asked.

[[speaker:sera]]“Why did you stop pursuit?”

Liang did not pretend not to understand.

[[speaker:liang]]“I saw him.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Rhen.”

[[speaker:liang]]“Yes.”

Sera waited.

Liang's face remained unreadable.

[[speaker:liang]]“You have misunderstood one thing.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Which thing?”

Liang looked at her.

[[speaker:liang]]“I did not spare you.”

Sera's eyes narrowed.

[[speaker:liang]]“I decided pursuing you was no longer worth dying for.”

That answer carried weight because of who said it.

World #2.

A woman who had killed a former #1.

A woman who did not flatter anyone.

Sera looked toward the place where Rhen had once knelt beside her unconscious body.

Frozen petals had not merely saved her.

They had ended pursuit because Liang Yue herself had chosen not to cross them.

title: Nine Borrowed Pulses
text:
Yan Shou's clinic occupied an abandoned imperial hospital.

Yan Shou — **The Red Ledger Physician** — had once served the imperial medical system before becoming custodian of the Concord's biological countermeasures. He was far weaker than Liang in direct combat. His threat came from turning patients, wounds and meridians into a network that punished anyone who tried to kill him carelessly.

Hundreds of patients rested inside.

Every one carried the same red wrist mark.

Yan greeted Liang politely.

He was older than his portraits.

Calm.

Almost gentle.

[[speaker:yan]]“If you kill me, they die.”

Liang's expression did not change.

Yan explained Nine Borrowed Pulses.

Artificial meridian bridges linked marked bodies into one physiological network.

Damage could be distributed.

Shock transferred.

Death shared.

Liang could kill Yan instantly.

That was never the problem.

The problem was doing so without killing everyone connected to him.

Yan smiled.

[[speaker:yan]]“You see the difficulty.”

Liang raised one finger.

Every red line beneath Yan's skin stopped moving.

He went pale.

She had already invaded his circulation.

[[speaker:liang]]“Do not confuse restraint with inability.”

Sera watched.

This was #2.

Yan's smile disappeared.

The hostages remained.

So Liang lowered her hand.

For now.

title: Bloodless Debt
text:
Yan activated his greatest revealed technique.

TRANSCENDED SKILL - BLOODLESS DEBT

Dozens of patients who had appeared healthy collapsed.

Old wounds.

Delayed hemorrhage.

Accumulated shock.

Every injury Yan had postponed was being called due at once.

Mei Zhen moved between patients faster than Sera had ever seen a physician move.

Liang controlled circulation in six bodies simultaneously.

Sera hunted hidden anchor operators.

Rhen remained still.

That frightened Yan more than movement would have.

Sera found the first anchor beneath a bell tower.

The second inside the hospital kitchen.

The third was a child.

Not an operator.

A victim.

Yan had designed the network so obvious solutions became moral traps.

Sera returned furious.

[[speaker:sera]]“I want him alive.”

Liang looked at her.

[[speaker:liang]]“Why?”

[[speaker:sera]]“So he understands losing.”

Liang almost smiled.

title: White Blood
text:
Yan attempted to escape through the eastern wing.

Liang followed.

He released forty pulse-linked guards.

Liang did not strike them.

She walked.

Every guard attacking her felt their own circulation betray the technique.

Knees weakened.

Grip failed.

Breath shortened.

No blood spilled.

No bodies flew through walls.

That made it worse.

The Bloodless Empress crossed the corridor while forty trained martial artists became physically incapable of completing an attack.

Yan stared.

[[speaker:yan]]“You cannot maintain that and protect the patients.”

Liang looked at him.

[[speaker:liang]]“Correct.”

Yan smiled.

Then noticed Sera behind him.

Liang had never needed to do both.

Sera's needle touched his neck.

[[speaker:sera]]“That's why there are two of us.”

The alliance between #2 and #7 was not equal in raw power.

It did not need to be.

They were solving different problems.

title: Empty Spring
text:
The network reached critical mass.

Hundreds of artificial meridian bridges lit beneath the city.

Mei Zhen stared at the map.

[[speaker:meizhen]]“If we cut them individually, we run out of time.”

Liang could suppress the system.

Not remove it without risking the real meridians underneath.

Rhen stepped forward.

Sera looked at him.

He placed two fingers against one red line.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Empty Spring.”

TRANSCENDED SKILL - EMPTY SPRING

Nothing exploded.

The artificial technique simply lost the principle that allowed it to exist.

One false bridge vanished.

Then another.

Then hundreds.

Real meridians remained untouched.

Yan Shou stopped breathing for an entirely different reason.

Liang Yue looked at Rhen.

For several seconds, World #2 said nothing.

Sera had learned that silence from a Duke could be louder than any compliment.

title: The White Funeral
text:
Yan's final defense was a sealed blood chamber linked to his heart.

Liang entered alone.

Sera did not argue.

This ending belonged to Liang.

Yan attacked with everything left.

Bloodless Debt.

Nine Borrowed Pulses.

Needle arrays.

Internal-force traps.

Liang walked through them.

Not because the techniques were weak.

Because she understood circulation better than the man who built them.

At the final exchange, Yan tried to transfer his fatal damage into one remaining hostage.

Liang severed the artificial pulse link before the thought completed.

Her palm stopped against his chest.

[[speaker:liang]]“You built medicine around fear.”

Yan trembled.

[[speaker:liang]]“That is why you never understood healing.”

She did not kill him.

Sera had asked for him alive.

Liang honored it.

That mattered to Sera more than she expected.

title: How Long Will You Stay
text:
The city recovered.

Mei Zhen remained to supervise patients.

Liang visited the tea shop once before leaving.

No other Duke was present.

No council.

No gathering.

Just Liang and Rhen.

[[speaker:liang]]“How long are you planning to stay this time?”

Rhen looked into his cup.

[[speaker:rhen]]“I don't know.”

Liang's eyes moved toward the stairs.

Sera's footsteps could be heard above.

[[speaker:liang]]“That's new.”

Rhen did not answer.

Liang stood.

Before leaving, she looked back.

[[speaker:liang]]“The Concord did not fear your techniques.”

Rhen's eyes lifted.

[[speaker:liang]]“It feared what nations become when they know you can decide their wars.”

The door closed.

Sera descended a moment later.

[[speaker:sera]]“What did she say?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“That the tea was acceptable.”

Sera threw a cloth at him.

title: The Second Seal
text:
Yan Shou's records identified the Second Seal.

Biological containment.

Medical networks.

Pulse-link systems.

Poisons designed not to kill powerful martial artists but to make overwhelming strength morally impossible.

Sera read until sunrise.

One phrase repeated through the records:

SURVIVE THE WINTER CATASTROPHE.

Rhen did not interrupt.

Finally Sera looked up.

[[speaker:sera]]“Did you ever actually lose control?”

Rhen's face became unreadable.

That frightened her more than a yes.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Not in the way they believed.”

[[speaker:sera]]“That is a very specific answer.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“It is the only one I have.”

Far away, military banners changed direction before their commanders issued orders.

An entire border army withdrew overnight.

On a hill above them, a man unfolded a paper map.

Yun Ke smiled.

The Third Seal had awakened.

The second seal closed with more questions than answers.
